title: Affinity-purification mass spectrometry on i) streptolysin O or C5a peptidase with human plasma or saliva; ii) human plasminogen with streptococcal proteins
projectDescription: In this project, we tried to use affinity-purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS) to study host-pathogen protein interaction, focusing initially on two major virulence factors of group A streptococcus (GAS), streptolysin O (SLO) and C5a peptidase (C5AP) with the immediate host microenvironment (human plasma or saliva); next centering on one major pathogenic host factor of GAS, human plasminogen (PLG) molecule with streptococcal cell-wall associate proteins (CAP) or secreted proteins (SP). Quantitative MS was performed in combination with interaction analysis to pinpoint the high-confidence interactive partner to the corresponding baits.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Affinity-enrichment assays were performed to characterise host-pathogen interactions using two experimental systems (interactomes A and B).  For interactome A, recombinant group A streptococcus (GAS) proteins, streptolysin O (SLO), C5a peptidase (C5AP), and a GFP control, were expressed in E. coli, purified, and immobilised on pre-washed Strep-Tactin Sepharose resin. Human plasma or saliva (Innovative Research) served as prey sources: plasma was additionally diluted to 50% (v/v) in PBS, and saliva was centrifuged and filtered prior to use. After repeated PBS washes to remove nonspecific binders, protein complexes were eluted with biotin, precipitated with trichloroacetic acid (TCA), washed with cold acetone, dried, and reconstituted in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate for in-solution digestion. Three experimental replicates were performed per bait–prey condition. For interactome B, native human plasminogen (Sigma-Aldrich) was immobilised on ECH-lysine beads (Cytiva) and incubated with prey fractions derived from Streptococcus pyogenes (M1 strain). The secreted protein fraction was obtained by centrifugation and concentration of bacterial culture supernatants, while the cell-wall-associated fraction was prepared by enzymatic digestion of bacterial pellets with mutanolysin and PMSF buffer. After incubation, columns were repeatedly washed with phosphate buffer containing 0.1 M NaCl, and complexes were eluted with 0.1 M NaCl plus 50 mM ε-aminocaproic acid. Eluates were processed via the same TCA precipitation and cleanup steps as for interactome A. Proteins were denatured in urea, reduced with tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP), alkylated with iodoacetamide, and digested overnight with trypsin (1:20 w/w). Peptides were desalted using C18 spin columns. For interactome B, both protein fractions were further fractionated using a High-pH Fractionation Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to improve detection of low-abundance peptides. Peptides were dried and reconstituted in buffer A (2% acetonitrile, 0.2% formic acid) for LC–MS analysis. We acknowledge the experimental contribution of Mr. Dongnian Han to the construction of interactome B during his master’s thesis project in the Malmström Lab, supervised by PhD student Di Tang in 2023. Mass spectrometric analyses were performed on an EASY-nLC 1200 system coupled to a Q Exactive HF-X Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).  For interactome A, peptides were analyzed using a 90-minute DIA gradient (3–38% solvent B) at 350 nL/min. MS1 scans (390–1210 m/z) were acquired at 60,000 resolution (AGC 3e6, 100 ms), followed by MS2 scans with a 26 m/z window at 30,000 resolution (AGC 1e6, 120 ms, NCE 30). For interactome B, both DDA and DIA modes were applied. DDA analysis used a 120-minute gradient (5–38% solvent B), MS1 scans at 60,000 resolution (350–1650 m/z, AGC 3e6, 50 ms), and top-20 MS2 scans at 15,000 resolution (AGC 1e5, 25 ms, NCE 27). DIA acquisition employed a 90-minute gradient with MS1 scans at 120,000 resolution (AGC 3e6, 60 ms) followed by 44 MS2 scans at 30,000 resolution (AGC 3e6) and stepped NCE values (25.5, 27, 30).
dataProcessingProtocol: For quantitative proteomics, a predicted spectral library was built from proteome UP000005640 (interactome A), and a hybrid spectral library combining DIA and DDA data was generated from proteome UP000000750 (interactome B) using FragPipe. DIA-NN was used for database searching and quantification, with inter-run normalization disabled to reflect the bait-specific enrichment design.  A bait–prey quantification matrix was created for each condition and analyzed using the MiST (Mass Spectrometry Interaction STatistics) algorithm, integrating abundance, specificity, and reproducibility metrics. High-confidence interactions were defined as those with MiST scores > 0.75.
